title: 500 Tbps Real-Time FinOps Streaming Pipeline with Zero-Copy eBPF
subtitle: Kernel-Bypass Ingestion, 95th Percentile Bandwidth Billing Optimization and SIMD Parsing
problem_statement: A global capital markets transaction logging platform ingests 500 Terabits per second of raw order streams across 12 exchanges. User-space Linux socket packet copies and cloud provider inter-region network egress costs create an unsustainable $1.8M/month cloud bill and trigger kernel packet drops.

faded_bug.description: Processing streaming packets in user-space requires multiple memory copies between kernel ring buffers and JVM heap.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
+ // Attach eBPF XDP program directly to network interface ring buffer
+ xdp.Attach(dev, xdp.WithFlags(xdp.DriverMode))

invariants.description: 95th percentile egress bandwidth and compute cost must remain strictly under monthly budget cap.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain how eBPF XDP (eXpress Data Path) processes packets at the NIC driver layer before allocating an `sk_buff` in the Linux kernel.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: How does 95th-percentile (burstable) bandwidth billing work? How does your ingestion scheduling shave the top 5% peak spikes to save hundreds of thousands of dollars?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: Under a 500 Tbps UDP flood, how does XDP drop malicious packets without consuming CPU cycles in userspace?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Design SIMD-accelerated JSON/binary parsing using AVX-512 instructions to eliminate CPU deserialization bottlenecks.

counter_probes.counter_question: At 500 Terabits per second, user-space context switches and memory copies saturate CPU cache lines within milliseconds. How can user-space runtimes handle this volume?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: They cannot. At hundreds of Tbps, kernel-bypass technologies (eBPF XDP, DPDK, AF_XDP) and hardware NIC offloads are mandatory to achieve zero-copy packet processing.
